questions.question: How does Spring Data JPA know what query to run for List<Book> findByAuthor(String author)?
options: It reads a hidden SQL file with the same name
It builds the query from the method name when the app starts
It runs findAll and filters in Java
It asks the database to guess
questions.explanation: The name is split into a start word and property names, and the query is derived from them at startup.

questions.question: Which method finds books priced from 250 up to 350, both included?
options: findByPriceBetween(int low, int high)
findByPriceInside(int low, int high)
findByPriceRange(int low)
findByPriceLessThan(int low, int high)
questions.explanation: The Between keyword takes two arguments, the low and the high limit, in that order.

questions.question: A repository has findTop2ByOrderByPriceDesc(). The prices are 350, 275, 420, 199, 310 and 150. Which prices come back?
questions.explanation: Top2 limits the result to two rows, and OrderByPriceDesc puts the highest prices first.

questions.question: The repository has List<Book> findByAuthour(String author), but the entity field is author. What happens?
options: It returns an empty list every time
It works and ignores the typo
The application fails at startup because no property named authour exists
It only fails when the method is called
questions.explanation: Spring Data checks method names against entity fields at startup and stops with a clear message.

questions.question: A search method can match many books, but it is declared as Book findByGenre(String genre). What is the likely problem?
options: It always returns the last book
It throws an error when more than one row matches, so it should return a List
It returns null for every genre
It sorts the books by title
questions.explanation: A single-object return type expects at most one row, so many matches cause an exception.
